clue.text: Salve keeping City still

indicators.note: keeping means the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: a salve is a soothing ointment, a balm
EC is the postcode for the City of London

explanation.surface: An ointment that keeps a city calm and quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district; 'keeping' puts its postcode inside the ointment.
explanation.definitionFit: To still the waters is to make them calm, as a ship is left motionless by windless weather.

clue.text: Players, each flanking very small River Dart

parts.note: a group of musicians playing together is a band

indicators.note: flanking means the first piece sits either side of the second

parts.note: a rill is a tiny stream

explanation.surface: A band of players beside a tiny stream on the river Dart in Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: The River Dart in Devon is the false trail: 'Dart' is the definition, a dart thrust into a bull in a bullfight.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullfighter's decorated barbed dart is planted in the bull's shoulders during the corrida.

clue.text: Bold Provençal city piercing confessor's heart

indicators.note: piercing means the city's name breaks into the other letters
the heart of a word is its central letters

parts.note: Arles is a city in Provence

explanation.surface: A daring southern French city that strikes at the core of a priest hearing confession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' takes the central three letters of the nine-letter word; 'piercing' breaks the city in after their second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bold shows no fear, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Shed for dog

definitions.meaning: Shed is the pseudonym of this puzzle's compiler, the one who devised the clues
a breed of gun dog, such as the Irish red one

explanation.surface: A garden shed being used as a kennel.
explanation.walkthrough: Shed is the setter's own name, so the self-reference supplies one sense; the other is the breed of dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Shed compiles this crossword, and the same word names a pointing gun dog breed.

clue.text: Sidle out drunk to get freedom from company

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters stagger about into a new order

explanation.surface: A drunk sneaks out of the pub to be left alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alone means being free of other people's company.

clue.text: American sailors on top in underworld

indicators.note: in a down clue, on top puts the sailors above the other piece

parts.note: tar is slang for a sailor; two of them give two tars

explanation.surface: US Navy sailors on top of the criminal underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth it is the deepest abyss of Hades, so a name for the underworld.

clue.text: Prince sheltering insurrectionary flower

indicators.note: sheltering means the prince's name wraps round the other piece

parts.note: Hal is Prince Henry, the future Henry V in Shakespeare
an insurrectionary is a rebel

explanation.surface: A prince hiding a rebel, perhaps in some flower bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Hal is Shakespeare's young Henry V.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a blue bell-shaped wild flower, a type of campanula.

clue.text: Part of cartel banished to island

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some cartel members are exiled to an island, as Napoleon was.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the Mediterranean island off Tuscany where Napoleon was exiled.

clue.text: Vegetable that's not initially glossy

indicators.note: not initially means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: sleek means smooth and glossy

explanation.surface: A vegetable that has lost its shine at first.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an onion-family vegetable, an example of the class.

clue.text: Rope has number in Lithuania

indicators.note: in puts the number inside the country's code

parts.note: LT is the international code for Lithuania
a number is a song, such as an aria in opera

explanation.surface: A rope with a figure on it, found in Lithuania.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is a musical number, a song, not a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a lasso, a long noosed rope used for catching animals.

clue.text: Lovely, fit woman included

indicators.note: included means the woman's name goes inside the other piece

parts.note: fit and able both mean capable
Dora is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A lovely, healthy woman is part of the group.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adorable is charming and lovely, a close synonym.

clue.text: Magician's impulse to follow short article on gold carpet

indicators.note: to follow means the impulse comes after the other pieces
short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: the is the definite article
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a mat is a small carpet
an urge is an impulse

explanation.surface: A magician feels an urge to write a short article about a golden carpet, perhaps a flying one.
explanation.definitionFit: A wonder-worker, from the Greek for a performer of marvels, is a word for a sorcerer.

clue.text: Tat creator created from clay

indicators.note: created means the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: A maker of cheap tat made something out of clay.
explanation.definitionFit: It is brownish-red fired clay used for pots and tiles.

clue.text: Training to put turn in charge

indicators.note: in places the turn inside the charge

parts.note: a charge is a price asked
a turn is an act on stage

explanation.surface: Training to put someone in charge of their turn.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'turn' is a variety act, as in a music-hall turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Practice is repeated exercise to improve a skill, which is training.

clue.text: 4 across's 4 across, perhaps, 4 across to leave skin infection

parts.note: the clue's setter speaking of himself is I, and 's stands for is
a setter dog is an example of a pet
the setter refers to himself as I
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Shed's dog is about to depart with a skin condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 across is SETTER: the setter is I, so 'setter's' is I'M; a setter dog is a pet; 'setter to leave' is I GO.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a contagious bacterial infection of the skin, common in children.

clue.text: Musician's introduction to dark stranger

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its first letter

parts.note: rum means odd, so rummer is stranger

explanation.surface: A musician's song introduces a tall, dark stranger.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Musician's stands for 'is'. 'rum' is British slang for odd.
explanation.definitionFit: A percussionist who plays drums is one kind of musician.

clue.text: Tie knot round record, getting head wiped, and go badly wrong

indicators.note: round means the wedding verb goes around the other piece

parts.note: to tie the knot is to marry

indicators.note: having its head wiped means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

explanation.surface: Someone fumbles tying a knot around a record and ends up wiping a head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting head wiped' takes D from DISC, leaving ISC.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans that miscarry fail, going wrong in their outcome.

clue.text: Desire to drink for five years

parts.note: lust is strong desire
rum is a drink

explanation.surface: A craving for alcohol lasting half a decade.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a Latin-derived term for a period of five years.

clue.text: Braggadocio's to traumatise a 4 across, stifling cry of pain

parts.note: to scar someone is to traumatise them

indicators.note: stifling means the first piece smothers the cry inside it

parts.note: the setter is me, speaking of himself
ouch is a cry of pain

explanation.surface: A boaster sets out to wound the setter, who has to stifle a yelp.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 across is SETTER, giving ME. The 's of Braggadocio's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the boastful, cowardly clown of the commedia dell'arte, a byword for empty bragging.

clue.text: Blouse shredded by dagger

indicators.note: shredded means the letters are torn up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A blouse slashed with a knife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shredded' rearranges BLOUSE. The dagger is the printer's mark, not a knife.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a printer's mark, either the dagger sign or the division sign.

clue.text: Prophet giving drug up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: soma is the drug in Brave New World

explanation.surface: A prophet hands out drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: He is an Old Testament prophet with a book of the Bible named after him.

clue.text: Make incomplete husks

indicators.note: incomplete means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a make of goods is a brand

explanation.surface: Leave the husks half-finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' is a noun here, a make of car.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the husks of grain separated from flour.

clue.text: Map-maker finding flashy car on a hill

parts.note: a Merc is a Mercedes, a showy car
a tor is a rocky hill

explanation.surface: A cartographer comes across a smart car on a hilltop.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerardus Mercator devised the famous map projection, so he was a cartographer.

clue.text: Sign of stone in Italy

parts.note: a gem is a precious stone
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A sign made of stone found in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a sign of the zodiac, the Twins.

clue.text: Girl from Spain retrospectively makes amends, receiving religious instruction

indicators.note: receiving means the reversed word takes the other piece inside
retrospectively means looking backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: atones means makes amends

explanation.surface: A Spanish girl looks back and makes amends after a religion lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrospectively' turns the amends word round to SENOTA; 'receiving' takes the abbreviation inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the Spanish term for a young unmarried woman.

clue.text: Garment for old flame back in house, mostly

indicators.note: in places the former partner inside the other piece
mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: the Tudors were an English royal house

indicators.note: back means the word is read the other way

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: A garment for an ex who has come back into the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses EX to XE; 'mostly' takes R from TUDOR, the dynasty of Henry VIII.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a dinner jacket, a man's formal evening garment.
